[PATH:empirical] Ongoing benchmarks for AGI-like capabilities (e.g., ARC-AGI, MMLU, and other general intelligence tests) tracked over the next 5-10 years — Systematic performance trends on these benchmarks can indicate whether AI systems are progressing toward general problem-solving abilities at a rate consistent with achieving AGI within 20 years.

[PATH:theoretical] Meta-analysis of historical AI capability scaling laws and compute trends (e.g., from papers by Kaplan et al. and Sutton's 'Bitter Lesson') — Extrapolating from compute, data, and model size scaling trends can provide a theoretical upper bound on when AGI might be achievable, given current hardware and algorithmic constraints.

[PATH:literature] Survey of expert forecasts and Delphi studies on AGI timelines (e.g., AI Impacts, recent surveys of AI researchers) — Aggregating and analyzing expert opinions can reveal consensus or divergence on the 20-year timeline, and identify key assumptions or breakthroughs that would confirm or refute the hypothesis.
